title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). P_n is the regular n-gon viewed as a map (carte) on the sphere: n vertices on the equator and two faces. Σ_{P_n} is the corresponding Riemann sphere. D_{P_n} is its dihedral automorphism group of order 2n, acting holomorphically on Σ_{P_n} ≅ P^1. \tilde P_{2n} is a chosen degree-2 cover of P_n (presumably the 2n-gon, z ↦ z^2). V_{\tilde P_{2n}} is a 2-dimensional complex vector space with Σ_{P_n} ≅ P(V_{\tilde P_{2n}})(C). D_{\tilde P_{2n}} is a central extension of D_{P_n} by {±1}, the pull-back of 1→{±1}→SL(V)→PGL(V)=Aut(Σ)→1.

The previous page argues as follows. When n is even, D^+_{\tilde P_{2n}} ≅ Z/2n → Z/n ≅ D^+_{P_n} does not split, so the extension does not split. Hence the projective action of D_{P_n} on Σ ≅ P^1 does not lift to a linear action.

This page restates that conclusion in sheaf language. The action does not lift to the pair (Σ_{P_n}, O(1)), with O(1) the degree-1 invertible sheaf (for instance the one coming from P(V)). In other words, the D_{P_n}-action admits no linearization of O(1). The obstruction is the nonzero class in H^2(D_n, C^*) = Z/2 for n even.

Grothendieck then introduces the principal C^*-bundle (12): PΣ_{P_n} = V̌(O(1))^*. This is the line bundle O(-1) with its zero section removed, i.e. canonically V_{\tilde P_{2n}} \ {0} → P(V). Consequences:
- D_{P_n} has no natural action on PΣ_{P_n}.
- Once the double cover \tilde P_{2n} is chosen (which pins down O(1) as coming from V_{\tilde P_{2n}}), the central extension D_{\tilde P_{2n}} acts on (12) through its linear action on V.

In all cases (n odd or even) he wants three things:
- the restriction (13): PΣ^*_{P_n} = PΣ_{P_n}|Σ^*_{P_n}, where Σ^* is the sphere minus the marked points of the map. This is a C^*-torsor over the punctured sphere, i.e. C^2 minus k lines through the origin;
- its fundamental groupoid with the D_{\tilde P_{2n}}-action;
- per the next page, the mixed fundamental group, with the action of D_{\tilde P_{2n}} × {1,τ}, where τ is complex conjugation.

Since Σ^* is an open curve, the torsor is trivial topologically. So π_1(PΣ^*) ≅ Z × F_{k-1}, a central extension of π_1(Σ^*) by Z = π_1(C^*). For k = 3 this is the pure braid group P_3.

Purpose: replace the dihedral-symmetric punctured sphere by a canonical-up-to-choice C^*-torsor carrying a genuine (metaplectic) group action. Then study the Galois/conjugation action on the associated Z-central extension of the profinite π_1, as part of the 'Teichmüller tower' programme for genus 0 with symmetries.
errors: Slight imprecision: even for n odd, where a linearization exists, it is not unique; it can be twisted by Hom(D_n, C^*) ≅ Z/2. So 'no natural action' holds for all n, which the text implicitly acknowledges by passing to D_{\tilde P_{2n}} in all cases.

Possible confusion in the identification of D_{\tilde P_{2n}}, from the previous page. If it is the preimage of D_{P_n} in SL_2 (the binary dihedral group), the extension never splits, even for n odd, since that group has a unique involution. The splitting for n odd holds for the automorphism group of the 2n-gon (D_{2n} ≅ D_n × Z/2), which acts on V through GL rather than SL. The two descriptions differ, though the conclusion on this page (an action of the order-4n extension on V \ {0}) is fine either way.

ideas.what: The projective dihedral action on P^1 is non-linearizable on O(1) for n even; the obstruction is the Schur multiplier class
ideas.modern_name: Linearization of group actions on line bundles; Schur multiplier H^2(D_n,C^*)=Z/2

ideas.what: Replacing P^1 by the C^*-torsor O(-1)\0 = V\{0}, on which a central extension of the symmetry group acts
ideas.modern_name: Metaplectic/central extension acting on the tautological C^*-torsor (cone over P^1)

ideas.what: Studying the fundamental groupoid and the mixed (arithmetic) fundamental group of the C^*-torsor over the punctured sphere, with the action of the finite symmetry group times complex conjugation
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on π_1 of complements of line arrangements in C^2 (Z-central extensions of genus-0 π_1, cf. P_3 ≅ Z×F_2); equivariant arithmetic fundamental groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura, Matsumoto (Galois actions on braid/mapping class groups); Grothendieck Esquisse for the general programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and Galois action but not, to my knowledge, this specific C^*-torsor construction

missed.claim: Programme to study the Galois (and complex-conjugation) action on the profinite π_1 of the C^*-torsor PΣ^*_{P_n} (≅ C^2 minus lines through 0) equivariantly for the order-4n central extension of the dihedral symmetry group of the n-gon map. This is a 'framed'/central-extension refinement of the Galois action on genus-0 fundamental groups with dihedral symmetry.
missed.quote: De façon précise, je m'intéresse au groupoïde fondamental de PΣ*_{P_n} et l'action de D_{\tilde P_{2n}} dessus
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The Z-central extension gives a cheap model of braid-type groups. Equivariance under binary/dihedral extensions relates to the Galois action on central extensions of mapping class groups and to dihedral symmetries of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller action. The equivariant, framed version appears only sporadically in the literature, but this is a modest, mostly routine set-up.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mainly a set-up. The non-linearizability for n even is a standard Schur-multiplier fact, and the C^*-torsor is the tautological one. The only mildly interesting element is the intended study of the equivariant mixed π_1 of this torsor; it is an unfinished thread, but close to known work on Galois actions on braid groups.

'et sur [-le groupe[?]-]' — the struck word may be 'le groupoïde' rather than 'le groupe'.
